'''Sōma Ōta Shrine''' (相馬太田神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Minamisōma|en|Minamisōma|qid=Q642094|lt=Minamisōma}}, {{ill|Haramachi-ku|ja|原町区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haramachi Ward|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24892679}}, Nakada Ōta. It is one of the three Myōken shrines associated with the Sōma clan and is also known as '''Ōta Shrine'''. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}}.

== Overview ==
The shrine traces its origins to the early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} during the Shōhei era (931–937), when {{ill|Taira no Masakado|2=en|3=Taira no Masakado|4=ja|5=平将門|6=de|7=Taira no Masakado|8=es|9=Taira no Masakado|10=fr|11=Taira no Masakado|lt=Taira no Masakado|qid=Q1207652|ja|Taira no Masakado|2=en|3=Taira no Masakado|4=ja|5=平将門|6=de|7=Taira no Masakado|8=es|9=Taira no Masakado|10=fr|11=Taira no Masakado|lt=Taira no Masakado|qid=Q1207652|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Masakado|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Masakado|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, an ancestor of the {{ill|Sōma clan|en|Sōma clan|qid=Q2975379|lt=Sōma clan}}, established a Myōken shrine at Moriyajō in Shimōsa Province's Sarushima District.

{{ill|Q11582495|ja|相馬師常|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Moritsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11582495}}, a twelfth-generation descendant of Masakado, received land in Mutsu Province after serving under {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}} during campaigns against the {{ill|Northern Fujiwara|en|Northern Fujiwara|qid=Q1050942|lt=Ōshū Fujiwara}}. Moritsune adopted the Sōma name from a cadet branch of the {{ill|Chiba clan|en|Chiba clan|qid=Q2975237|lt=Chiba clan}}, becoming the first lord of Sōma in Mutsu.

Later, in Genkyō 3 (1321) on April 22, {{ill|Q11582542|ja|相馬重胤|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Shigetane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11582542}} relocated from Moriyajō in Shimōsa Province to this area. He enshrined the clan deity, Myōken, establishing the current shrine.

The Sōma clan, strong adherents of Myōken faith, brought their revered deity from Shimōsa to this site. The Myōkendō (Myōken Hall) became the basis of what is now Sōma Ōta Shrine.

The shrine has been venerated as the tutelary deity of the {{ill|Sōma clan|en|Sōma clan|qid=Q2975379|lt=Sōma clan}} and served as the clan's ancestral shrine.

== Major Events ==
During the annual {{ill|Sōma Nomaoi|ja|相馬野馬追|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Nomaoi|qq=}}, nighttime ceremonies for riders are held at various Myōken shrines.

On {{ill|Ōmisoka|en|Ōmisoka|qid=Q2357104|lt=New Year’s Eve}}, the shrine conducts traditional performances of shell horn blowing, continuing into the early hours of New Year's Day.

== Important Cultural Properties ==
{{ill|Sōma Nomaoi|ja|相馬野馬追|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Nomaoi|qq=}} is designated as a National {{ill|National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|重要無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q6573893}}, and other items are registered as tangible folk cultural properties by Minamisōma City:
* Battle drums used in Sōma Nomaoi
* Painted horse illustrations on ema (votive plaques)
* Feathered spears
* Stone pagodas
